title: Duffy's Tavern
paragraphs: A character comedy set around New York's Duffy's Tavern, where fast-talking manager Archie schemes, argues with the regulars, and tries to impress a steady stream of celebrity guests.
Situation comedy set in the fictional Duffy's Tavern, managed by Archie for the never-heard owner Duffy.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS era (July 29, 1940 to June 30, 1942), Blue Network era (October 6, 1942 to June 27, 1944), NBC era (September 15, 1944 to December 28, 1951), and Puerto Rico production era (1949 to December 28, 1951).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|ed-gardner|Ed Gardner]] (performer, director, and producer), Charlie Cantor (performer), [[person|eddie-green|Eddie Green]] (performer), Matty Malneck and His Orchestra (performer), Hazel Shermet (performer), Larry Rhine (writer), and Florence Halop (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], and [[org|org.0e05223f9d198710|Nostalgia Broadcasting Corporation]].

The stories often return to tavern business and neighborhood social life, celebrity guests and show-business culture, Archie schemes and get-rich plans, music and live entertainment, dating, courtship and romantic pursuit, and money, debt, prices and business problems.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Neighborhood tavern as recurring American radio-comedy setting, Eddie Green and positive Black radio characterization, Puerto Rico tax-incentive production migration, and Celebrity guest culture in network radio comedy.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-fred-allen-show|The Fred Allen Show]], [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]], and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]].
